TEMG 1010.title: T&M Professional Activities
TEMG 1010.description: A compulsory course for students enrolling in the Dual Degree Program in Technology and Management throughout their five years of study. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students, to enhance their personal and professional skills, to improve their understanding of latest business and technology development and to improve their communication skills. Activities involve executive forums, workshops and mentoring program. Graded P or F.
cilos: Improve students’ understanding of latest business and technology development.
Develop students’ presentation and communication skills.

TEMG 3950.title: T&M Case Analysis and Product Innovation
TEMG 3950.description: TEMG3950 is divided into 2 parts. Part 1 is "Case Analysis" for students to develop structured problem-solving skills using MECE frameworks and communicate solution using 5-Step Persuasive Selling in essay and presentation format. Part 2 is "Product Innovation" for students to develop critical thinking skills using techniques such as Design Thinking. Value Proposition Design and Business Model Canvas. Instructor consent is needed for this course.
cilos: Understand the basic concepts and methods in consulting industries.
Understand the basic theories and skills in problem identification & framing.
Design, prototype and evaluate an interactive business plan via case study.
Communicate effectively with target clients and different stakeholders in real business setting.
Analyze potential impact and benefits of business plan via case study.
Master the Design Thinking process.
Apply design thinking methodology to problem solving.

TEMG 4000.title: Special Topics
TEMG 4000.description: Selected topics of current interest in Technology and Management. May be repeated for credits if different topics are covered.
cilos: Evaluate and analyze the commercial potential of inventive ideas using business modeling skills and market assessment techniques.
Apply and develop higher-order strategic thinking skills to create comprehensive commercialization strategies for innovative concepts.
Identify and justify target markets, analyze competition, and formulate growth strategies for inventive ideas in various industries.
Develop sales channel, distribution, projections and resource allocation plans, demonstrating financial acumen in the context of commercializing innovations.
Articulate and present commercialization plans, including go-to-market strategies and implementation roadmaps for inventive ideas.

TEMG 4940.title: T&M Prototyping and Research Project
TEMG 4940.description: TEMG4940 series of project-based courses is for T&M-DDP students to gain deep insight into an industry domain by working with corporate-sponsor(s) to understand a new trend in the industry, appreciate the business challenges behind the problem, and develop a working prototype incorporating innovative business strategies and advanced software tools. Students may repeat the course for credits if the topics are different. Instructor consent is required for this course.
cilos: Acquire insight into project sponsor’s organization and empathy with their challenges.
Become familiar with technology trends and industry landscape.
Gain confidence to apply problem solving techniques covered in the course.
Improve professional communication in writing and public speaking.
Improve teamwork across cultures, age and disciplines.

TEMG 4950.title: T&M Corporate Consulting Project
TEMG 4950.description: TEMG 4950 series are experiential-learning courses where students role-play management consultants using technology & management (T&M) strategies to solve a complex problem currently faced by an industry leading firm. This project uses the format of a consulting engagement with at least 5 client meetings. Final solution recommendation will be presented before a panel of executives from the client’s organization, project sponsors and industry subject experts. Students are allowed to repeat TEMG 4950 projects with the projects covering different topics. Instructor consent is required for this course.
cilos: Acquire insight into project sponsor’s organization and empathy with their challenges.
Become familiar with technology trends and industry landscape.
Gain confidence to apply problem solving techniques covered in the course.
Improve professional communication in writing and public speaking.
Improve teamwork across cultures, age and disciplines.

TEMG 4970.title: T&M IBPC Startup Project
TEMG 4970.description: TEMG4970 International Business Plan Competition (IBPC) offers an opportunity for aspiring young students to work in a multi-discipline and multi-cultural environment to develop startup businesses leveraging breakthroughs in technology and business innovation to impact a lot of lives. Students may repeat the course for credits if the topics are different. Instructor consent is required for this course.
cilos: Improve awareness of latest trends in target tech sector and business applications.
Improve ability to apply Lean Launchpad Startup business planning.
Improve professional communication in writing and public speaking.
Improve teamwork across cultures, age and disciplines.
